---
title: "estiMINT: EIR and HBR"
---

Every model downstream requires an EIR. `estimint` supplies one, inverting either a parasite
prevalence or a biting rate into the entomological inoculation rate (EIR), and converting
between EIR and the human biting rate (HBR) in both directions.

What comes back is always a single equilibrium value rather than a trajectory, because the
trajectories come from [stateMINT](../05-statemint/index.qmd). The distinction is set out in
[EIR, HBR, prevalence, and cases](../03-concepts/equilibrium.qmd).

::: {.chapter-outline}
- [Nets and dn0](nets-and-dn0.qmd) — turn a net mix and a resistance level into the two numbers the models consume.
- [Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd) — the core inversion, and why a lookup table will not do.
- [EIR and HBR](eir-and-hbr.qmd) — the other two models, and the error a round trip through both accumulates.
- [Mosquito density and EIR](mosquito-density.qmd) — the effect of larviciding, or of a wetter climate, on transmission.
- [estiMINT API](api.qmd) — the inference surface, function by function.
:::

## The three models

`estimint` ships three gradient-boosted models inside the wheel. Nothing is downloaded. Each
maps one driving input to one output while holding the same six covariates fixed. Pick the
model by what you measured.

| Model name | Driving input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `"prevalence"` | `prev_y9` (parasite prevalence) | EIR |
| `"eir_to_hbr"` | `eir` | HBR |
| `"hbr"` | `hbr_y9` (human biting rate) | EIR |

A model is named for its *input*. The model named `"hbr"` takes an HBR as its driving input
and returns an EIR.

All three are loaded by name with `load_xgb_model` and called with `run_xgb_model`. The six
shared covariates (`dn0_use`, `Q0`, `phi_bednets`, `seasonal`, `itn_use` and `irs_use`) describe
the setting. Two of them are not survey quantities at all. `dn0_use` and `itn_use` come out of
`calculate_dn0`, which accounts for most of the errors made with the package. Start there, at
[Nets and dn0](nets-and-dn0.qmd).
